text:
devon: FYI support just escalated a customer complaining about a big p95/p99 regression after yesterday's runtime rollout. customer said tail latencies jumped ~4x and some 504s. tagging eng-runtime.

kevin: opening bridge, thanks. can you paste the customer request and the exact model + route they hit?

devon: customer payload: model=redwood-open-3b, route=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2. they provided approx timestamps: 2024-11-07T14:12:00Z -> 14:45:00Z.

maria: that timeframe overlaps with our canary rollout of runtime v2024.11.07 (sha: b7f3c9a). canary cohort was 10% across us-west-2. I already looked at the deploy bot notes: rollout-bot: canary started 2024-11-07T13:55 UTC, canary health OK -> promoted to 30% at 14:05, promotion paused at 14:30.

rollout-bot: Deployment b7f3c9a: canary -> 10% @13:55, 30% @14:05, paused @14:30 due to elevated p99 on canary nodes. See /deploy/ops-1234.

kevin: good. checking metrics now. running quick query for p95/p99 for route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-open-3b in us-west-2.

kevin: (run) `redwoodctl metrics query --route "/v1/generate" --model redwood-open-3b --region us-west-2 --from 2024-11-07T13:45 --to 2024-11-07T15:00 --granularity 1m`

kevin: output snippet: 
```
13:58 p95=120ms p99=210ms
14:06 p95=150ms p99=260ms
14:12 p95=320ms p99=980ms <-- spike starts
14:25 p95=380ms p99=1.2s
14:32 p95=140ms p99=230ms <-- after partial rollback on one canary pool
```

ashok: interesting. p95 rose first, then p99 exploded around 14:12. could be a scheduling or kernel selection issue causing stragglers. any error logs?

maria: pulled logs from canary pods: `kubectl -n runtime logs -l rollgroup=canary-b7f3 -c inference --since=1h`. found repeated gRPC deadlines and occasional OOM-ish GC stalls in runtime worker logs. sample: 
```
E 2024-11-07T14:13:02.123Z inference_worker.cpp:462 request_id=... kv_cache_miss=true kernel_selector=fast_attention_v2 latency=1190ms
W 2024-11-07T14:14:01.980Z grpc_server.cpp:210 deadline_exceeded tid=... "deadline exceeded while waiting for model kernel"
```

devon: kv_cache_miss=true stands out. was there any change to KV cache or cache sharding in this release?

maria: yes, b7f3c9a introduced two changes: (1) new kernel selector that prefers fast_attention_v2 on Ampere GPUs, (2) rebalanced KV cache shards to reduce memory footprint. Individually small but possible interaction.

kevin: let's try to bisect. can we reproduce on a single canary node by toggling kernel selector? we have feature flags.

ashok: I launched a canary playground instance in us-west-2 and toggled `runtime.feature.fast_attention_v2=false` via configmap. reran synthetic load with `wrk` and a small prompt set.

ashok: reproduction steps: 
```
# on canary node
kubectl -n runtime exec -it runtime-canary-4 -- /bin/bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/flags -d '{"fast_attention_v2": false}'
wrk -t2 -c50 -d60s http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -s generate.lua
```

ashok: result: p99 dropped back to ~220ms under the same synthetic workload. enabling `fast_attention_v2` again increased p99 to ~980ms within a minute.

maria: that strongly implicates fast_attention_v2 path. the KV cache rebalance might amplify misses but the kernel change seems primary.

kevin: can we do a targeted rollback of kernel selector without rolling back whole runtime? if not, do staged rollback of canary group.

maria: we don't have per-node kernel selector toggle at runtime-wide scale, only via configmap/flag per pool. I started rolling back the canary pool to previous image (sha: a9d4b1e) at 14:30 — that aligns with the metric dip at 14:32.

rollout-bot: Rollback initiated: group canary-b7f3 -> image a9d4b1e at 2024-11-07T14:30.

devon: customer updated: tail latencies improved after 14:35, they confirm errors stopped.

kevin: we should run a quick bisect locally to see minimal repro: is the crash triggered by sequence length or batch size? try load with longer prompt and small batch sizes.

ashok: ran matrix: sequence len 512 vs 1024; batch size 1 vs 8. Observed worst p99 when seq_len >=1024 and batch size >=4. logs show `kv_cache_miss` rate higher with larger sequences. hypothesis: fast_attention_v2 has a regression for large sequences leading to slow kernel fallback or cache thrash.

maria: filed an internal ticket: INFRA-4721 documenting reproduction, logs, and bisect. assigning to @ashok and cc @runtime-team.

ashok: adding to ticket: suggested immediate mitigations: (A) disable fast_attention_v2 by default in next canary, (B) revert KV cache sharding change for the affected model family, (C) add obs to track kernel_selector latency distribution.

kevin: agree. also add a metric alert for kernel_selector slow tail and kv_cache_miss rate so we catch earlier.

maria: opened PR to toggle off fast_attention_v2 in canary config and to add a canary-run test that runs long-sequence prompts under load. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/3182

devon: communicating to customer: told them we've rolled back canary, still investigating root cause, they'll get a follow-up within 24h. they asked for postmortem.

kevin: next steps: 1) keep canary rolled back until we release a patched kernel selector; 2) run extended soak tests with seq_len=2048 under load for 2 hours; 3) add targeted unit/integration tests for cache sharding interactions.

maria: I'll coordinate the soak and keep the incident label. assigning: ashok=investigate kernel code + repro, kevin=alerts/dashboards, devon=customer comms.

ashok: quick note — I reproduced locally inside the kernel runtime with perf trace; `fast_attention_v2` hits a slow path when `kv_cache_miss` ratio >0.3 causing a fallback to synchronous memcpy that blocks worker thread. attaching perf snippet in ticket.

kevin: thanks. marking this as Sev-2 for now. if customer impact grows we'll escalate.

devon: thanks all, I'll send the customer the rollback update and ETA for follow-up.

maria: posting a brief incident summary in #incidents and will schedule a short postmortem meeting tomorrow.

ashok: started a draft of the retrospective: timeline, repro steps, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, and test additions. will paste into INFRA-4721 once ready.

kevin: good work. let's keep this thread updated with any new findings or if the rollback shows any regressions.

devon: closing loop with customer at 14:52 — they confirmed improvement. will reopen if anything else. :thumbsup:
